script.opening_words:
Two retired couples live on the same
cul-de-sac in suburban Tampa. Both are
68, both worked 40 years, both retired
last spring with almost identical nest
eggs. From the driveway, you cannot tell
them apart. Couple A pulls in driving a
leased 2025 Lincoln Navigator. Behind it
sits a 32-foot Class A motorhome they've
used three weekends all year. The
mailbox just delivered an $1,800
country club statement. Yesterday, their
daughter's monthly $1,200
went out on Venmo. Couple B drives a
2014 Toyota
script.ending_words:
me lifestyle on the surface, but
couple B is going to die rich. And
couple A is going to spend the last five
years of their life quietly running the
numbers, wondering if they should sell
the lake house, wondering if they can
ask their daughter to stop accepting the
Venmos, wondering how the math got away
from them when they were so sure it
wouldn't.
The wealthy retirees who stay wealthy
don't have a secret. They have a list of
things they refuse to buy. Most people
watching this video will agree with
everything in it and then change
nothing. They'll buy the boat anyway,
the math doesn't care.
